prompt: A call center's cost per call rose 20%, while wages stayed the same. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Calls are probably taking longer as issues get more complex.
options.feedback: Right. With wages flat, cost per call rises when each call takes longer or agents sit idle. I'd check average handle time by call type.

options.text: Agents' pay has probably risen under a new contract.
A new phone system is slowing agents, so it has to be replaced.
options.feedback: Nothing mentions a new system, and this jumps to a fix before any data.

options.text: Call volumes have likely surged past what the team can take.
options.feedback: More calls would spread fixed costs and lower the cost per call. With wages flat, the extra cost has to come from time spent per call or idle time.

explanation: The data shows cost per call up 20% with wages flat, so each call takes more paid time. Likely cause: calls are taking longer as issues get more complex. To test it, check average handle time by call type. If handle time is flat, look at idle time and staffing instead.
